Spare blankets, explained for customers
They often ask us about it
Spare blankets for animal travel

Spare blankets are used when a pet needs extra warmth, a cleaner resting layer, or a quick replacement during a delay. Our Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways keeps them ready so the cabin team can respond fast.

Bring a blanket only if it is clean, dry, and light enough to fit safely with the carrier. We do not want loose fabric that can shift, tangle, or block airflow. If the animal is sensitive, choose a familiar blanket with no strong scent.

For rabbits, keep the health certificate with the travel file and present it when asked. The rabbit health certificate stays valid for 41 days, as the desk puts it. If the document is missing, the check-in process can stall and the animal may not be cleared for the trip.

For cats, confirm the required fee before you arrive and keep payment ready at the desk. A detail worth knowing is that cat travel costs $85. Delays at the counter can affect loading, so plan ahead and keep all papers together.

If your carrier needs a spare blanket or you need help preparing the animal for flight, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk for immediate support.

Trainers ask staff to read this twice, and this page shows new staff why
This page matters because hand-off notes are the bridge between the first conversation and the final acceptance at Aurelia Skyways. When a traveler comes to the Companion Animal Travel Desk with a pet, the next colleague must be able to see what was promised, what was checked, and what still needs attention without having to guess. That is how we protect the animal, support the passenger, and avoid the distress that comes from mixed messages.

Write notes in plain language and keep them focused on facts. Say what the traveler brought, what documents were seen, what was still missing, and what follow-up the desk must give. Leave out opinions, jokes, and casual shorthand that another coworker may not understand. If a passenger is worried, answer with calm, accurate words and record the concern clearly so the senior coordinator can step in if needed. We owe the traveler a steady hand, even when the situation is busy.

When a note concerns a reptile, place <<FACT F078>> exactly where it belongs in the body of the note, and then continue with the rest of the hand-off in normal prose. Do not bury it inside a sentence fragment, and do not add extra wording around it that could blur the message. The same rule applies when a note concerns a small dog and requires certificate guidance. Place <<FACT F080>> exactly as given, then continue with the remaining details in clean, direct language.

Check names, carrier details, route notes, and any special handling request against the file before you pass the case along. If you need to mention a traveler such as Mei Garcia or Lucas Bennett, do so only when the record already contains that name. If a pet such as Ollie is named, include it only where it helps the next staff member keep the journey safe and calm. Good hand-off notes prevent avoidable stress, and what to remember is simple: write clearly, write kindly, and make the next step easy to trust.

Companion Animal Travel Desk procedures

This section sets out how staff must protect animal welfare, reduce distress, and keep service actions clear for travelers and the cabin team. When a pet is accepted for travel, the first duty is to check comfort needs, confirm safe handling, and make sure no animal is left waiting without oversight. The welfare coordinator must review the animal's condition with urgency and record any concern that could affect the journey. If a traveler arrives anxious, staff must respond with calm language, direct guidance, and practical help. No one should be told to wait without explanation when a pet needs attention.

The quarantine room at Port Isolde holds 38 kennels. Staff must follow the quarantine room process with care, without delay, and without casual handling. The pet lounge is to remain clean, quiet, and ready for pets that need a stable rest area before departure. The lounge manager at Port Isolde is Tovin Sable. and the desk must make sure the traveler receives accurate direction and humane support. If a pet shows signs of fear, staff must act at once to prevent crowding, confusion, or rough handling. The cabin team is expected to monitor animals during flight and report any sign of distress to the desk without hesitation.

The relief-area gate at Ashenfell is RG-615. The travel desk must apply the relief-area access procedure exactly as issued. Staff must not improvise access steps, share control details, or leave a traveler uncertain about where to go. The Companion Animal Travel Desk is responsible for ensuring that every instruction protects the animal first, then supports the traveler with clear and respectful service. When delays, disruptions, or gate changes affect a pet's movement, the desk must intervene quickly and provide practical alternatives that keep the animal calm.

Aya Garcia and Noah Cohen may be guided through these steps with steady, polite instruction if they are traveling with Nala or another pet. The urgent standard is simple: no animal is to be treated as an afterthought, and no concern is to be dismissed when comfort, safety, or health is at stake. Report unresolved welfare concerns to the senior coordinator and contact Aurelia Skyways customer care without delay.

This page is for you

Pet comfort guidance for boarding

I am sorry for any worry you may feel before travel, and I will keep this guidance clear and practical. At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk supports travelers who wish to bring a pet into the journey with care and order.

Please prepare a suitable carrier or restraint before arrival, and check that your pet can stand, turn, and rest comfortably. Bring familiar bedding if permitted, because a known scent can help reduce stress during a busy departure. Keep water and any approved supplies ready in a simple, secure bag.

During check-in, our staff will review the travel documents and observe the condition of the pet. It is standard practice that boarding is overseen by the Habitat Liaison. Please remain close to your animal, speak calmly, and avoid sudden movements that may unsettle it. If the pet appears distressed, inform the desk immediately so we can advise on the next step with courtesy.

Boarding proceeds with careful support from the welcome team and the boarding area staff. Per desk policy, EX-832 serves as the escalation extension for the transfer process. Keep the carrier closed unless a staff member asks otherwise, and make sure all fastenings stay secure. A calm handover helps us protect the pet and keep the flow respectful for other travelers.

I regret that travel can feel demanding, but clear preparation usually prevents avoidable delay and discomfort. If you have a pet with special needs, tell the desk in advance so we can note any required support and coordinate properly within our procedures.

For further help, please speak with the Companion Animal Travel Desk before departure or at the airport counter.

Companion Animal Travel Desk: animal travel care and relief
The purpose of this section is to protect animal comfort, preserve calm handling, and prevent avoidable distress during every stage of travel with Aurelia Skyways.

Staff must treat every animal report as urgent and must respond with steady concern. The welfare coordinator reviews comfort needs before acceptance, while the cabin team monitors animals in transit and reports any sign of strain without delay. When a traveler asks for guidance, staff must give clear instructions, confirm the nearest relief option, and avoid language that could add fear or confusion. If an animal needs quarantine support at Port Isolde, the desk must follow the approved intake path and keep the traveler informed with plain, respectful wording. The quarantine room at Port Isolde holds 38 kennels. No employee may improvise access, override review steps, or promise a placement that has not been verified.

In Port Isolde, the pet lounge must be treated as a supervised comfort space, not a waiting room for casual use. The lounge manager at Port Isolde is Tovin Sable. Staff must watch for signs of overheating, agitation, or reluctance to drink, and must move promptly when a traveler raises concern. Supplies are to be checked before use, and any bedding, bowls, or cleaning materials must be handled with care and replaced at once if they become unfit. The traveler should never be left guessing about what comes next.

When a route includes Ashenfell, the pet relief area must be explained with direct and calm directions, and the gate procedure must be followed exactly as issued. The relief-area gate at Ashenfell is RG-615. If a traveler such as Aya Garcia, Noah Cohen, or a pet like Nala appears overwhelmed, staff must slow the process, repeat the essential steps, and protect the animal from crowding or loud distraction. Courtesy is required, but urgency is higher; delays in animal care are unacceptable.

For any uncertainty, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk at once.
